title: Reservation in promotion - the current legal position after recent rulings
p1: Can an employee claim reservation as a matter of right when seeking promotion in government service? The Supreme Court's position may surprise many people: the Constitution permits reservation in promotion, but does not make it compulsory.
p2: A common misconception is that reservation in promotion automatically follows reservation at the time of recruitment. That is not the law. Under Article 16(4A), the State has discretion to provide reservation in promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, subject to constitutional safeguards. No employee can demand it as an absolute fundamental right.
p3: The Supreme Court's decisions in M. Nagaraj, Jarnail Singh and the February 2025 ruling in Amrit Yadav reinforce this framework. Before introducing promotional reservation, the government must collect quantifiable data establishing inadequate representation in the relevant cadre. It must also consider administrative efficiency under Article 335. Importantly, proving the backwardness of SC/ST communities afresh is not required. The government must also respect applicable constitutional limits and ensure that its policy has a sound factual basis. Recent judicial scrutiny continues to emphasise that promotional benefits cannot be granted through arbitrary executive decisions.
conclusion: The real question is this: should reservation in promotion be primarily guided by social justice, or should measurable representation and administrative efficiency determine its extent? Where should the law draw the line? Share your perspective.
